md_name: Herbicide Compound Characterization and Bioactivity Workflow
md_description: This workflow covers lab synthesis of candidate herbicide compounds, their structural and physicochemical characterization by NMR and mass spectrometry, and in vitro testing against plant enzymes and cellular pathways. It produces raw spectral signals, derived compound identity annotations, assay readouts, and integrated potency/selectivity summaries to support agricultural candidate evaluation.

starting_reagents.reasoning: The starting_reagents node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the chemical precursors and reagents themselves, not synthesis parameters, purification details, capture settings, or assay outputs. Because this is the root material node, identifier-style fields are appropriate here and should not be repeated later; I avoided compound batch, product, or downstream analytical fields since those belong to process, capture, signal, or derivative nodes. I also kept the schema focused on what a downstream user needs to know to trace reagent provenance and composition for the synthesis step.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the reagent set used as the starting materials for herbicide synthesis; use a stable string such as 'SR-001'. Record at the reagent lot/batch level when multiple precursors are pooled into one starting material set.
Primary name of the starting chemical precursor or reagent, as recorded before synthesis begins; examples include an amine, acid chloride, heterocycle precursor, solvent, base, or coupling reagent.

Functional role of the material in the synthesis input set, recorded at the time the starting reagents are assembled; examples indicate whether the material is a precursor, coupling agent, catalyst, base, solvent, or additive.

Structured chemical identity for the starting material, such as common name, IUPAC name, or registry identifier; if available, include a stable identifier like an InChIKey or CAS number in the same text field.

Declared or measured purity of the starting reagent at receipt or before use in synthesis, reported as percent % w/w or molar purity when that is the laboratory convention; typical values are 0-100 and this helps assess input quality.
Vendor, internal source, or institution that supplied the starting reagent; record the source at receipt so the synthesis input provenance can be traced.
Supplier or internal lot/batch number for the starting reagent, recorded from the container label or inventory record; use a string format such as 'LOT-2024-015'.
Physical or formulation state of the starting reagent when used for synthesis; examples include solid, liquid, solution, or salt form. Record the state before any synthesis processing begins.

herbicide_synthesis.reasoning: The herbicide_synthesis node is a Process, so I included only synthesis-operation fields: protocol identity, reaction conditions, reagent use, duration, atmosphere, workup, and a process-level outcome/quality indicator. I excluded starting material identity and batch properties because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded crude product characterization, purification results, and downstream analytical or assay outputs because those belong to later Entity/Process/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any reagent-identifying fields already assigned to starting_reagents, focusing instead on how the transformation was performed and how successfully it proceeded.

md_schema.descr: Name or short label of the synthetic route used for this herbicide candidate; record the procedure used for the reaction run at the time synthesis begins, for example a literature method, internal SOP name, or project-specific route label.

Reaction temperature maintained during the synthesis step, reported in degrees Celsius as the actively controlled reaction condition; typical values may range from below 0 to above 100 depending on the route.
Total elapsed reaction time for the synthesis step, measured from reagent combination to quench/workup initiation, in minutes; record the actual run duration rather than planned duration.
Atmospheric condition used during synthesis, recorded as the actively controlled environment for the reaction vessel; for example inert gas purge, dry air, or ambient atmosphere.

Primary solvent or solvent mixture used during the synthesis reaction, recorded as the medium present during the transformation; include the solvent names in a single string such as 'THF/water' or 'DCM'.

Key catalytic or reagent additions used to drive the synthesis, recorded as the operational input set for the reaction; include approximate equivalents, catalytic loading, or stoichiometric excess in text when relevant.

Brief description of the immediate post-reaction workup or crude-isolation preparation performed at the end of synthesis before downstream purification, such as quench, extraction, filtration, or solvent removal.
Isolated or crude yield obtained from the synthesis step, reported as percent relative to the limiting reagent at the point the product batch is first recovered; typical values are 0-100.
Overall outcome of the synthesis operation, recorded after the run is completed and before purification; use this to indicate whether a usable crude batch was obtained.

crude_compound_batch.reasoning: The crude_compound_batch node is an Entity, so I included intrinsic properties of the synthesized mixture itself: composition, physical form, origin from the synthesis step, and quality indicators that describe the batch as received before purification. I excluded synthesis conditions because those belong to the upstream Process, and I excluded purified material properties, analytical measurements, capture settings, and downstream identity/assay outputs because those belong to later nodes. I also avoided repeating any reagent identifiers or synthesis yields already handled upstream, focusing on what the crude batch is and what its immediate state is before purification.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the crude herbicide compound batch obtained directly from synthesis and before purification; use a stable string such as 'CB-001'.
Reference to the synthesis run that produced this crude batch, recorded as the originating process identifier or label at the point the mixture is first collected.
Observed physical form of the crude batch before purification, recorded at collection; examples include oil, solid, foam, slurry, or solution.
Free-text description of the crude mixture composition before purification, including major product, detectable byproducts, residual reagents, or solvent carryover if known.

Estimated percentage of desired herbicide product in the crude batch prior to purification, reported as percent w/w or area percent depending on the lab convention; typical values range from 0 to 100.
Total recovered mass of the crude batch at the time of collection before purification, reported in milligrams; record the measured mass of the crude material as-is.
Condition used to hold the crude batch before purification, recorded at the time of storage or transfer; examples include refrigerated, frozen, desiccated, or ambient.
Qualitative assessment of crude batch suitability for purification, recorded after synthesis and visual inspection; use this to note whether the batch is acceptable for downstream purification.

compound_purification.reasoning: The compound_purification node is a Process, so I included only the purification/isolation operation details: method, solvents, fraction handling, conditions, duration, recovery, and process-level outcome quality. I excluded crude-batch intrinsic properties because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded analyte-ready compound properties, analytical identity, and downstream assay outputs because those belong to later Entity/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any synthesis or reagent identifiers from earlier nodes, focusing on how the crude material was converted into analyte-grade material and how effective that operation was.

md_schema.descr: Primary purification method used to isolate the herbicide compound, recorded at the time the crude batch is processed; examples include column chromatography, recrystallization, HPLC, liquid-liquid extraction, or solid-phase extraction.

Solvent or solvent mixture used during purification, recorded as the active mobile phase, wash, or recrystallization medium at the time the purification is performed; for example 'hexane/ethyl acetate' or 'water/acetonitrile'.

Temperature maintained during purification or isolation, reported in degrees Celsius as the actively controlled condition for the purification operation; typical values may span below 0 to room temperature or elevated temperatures for recrystallization.
Total elapsed time for the purification operation, measured from the start of crude-material handling to recovery of analyte-ready material, in minutes.
Identifier for the collected fraction or pooled fraction set when the purification is fraction-based; use a string or numeric label such as 'F3' or 'fraction_12'.

Percentage of desired compound recovered after purification and isolation relative to the crude batch or theoretical amount, reported at the point analyte-ready material is obtained; typical values range from 0 to 100.
Estimated purity of the isolated compound immediately after purification and before downstream characterization, reported as percent by the laboratory's standard method.
Overall success status of the purification run, recorded after isolation is complete; use this to indicate whether analyte-ready material meeting downstream requirements was obtained.

analyte_ready_compound.reasoning: I removed the colliding field purity_percent because already_generated indicates that an equivalent purity field was already produced for an earlier node in the DAG. The remaining fields stay within the Entity territory of analyte_ready_compound by describing intrinsic identity, physical form, salt form, storage, available mass, and readiness for downstream characterization, while avoiding capture, process, signal, or derivative information.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified herbicide material prepared for analytical characterization and bioassays; use a stable string such as 'AC-001'.

Name or project label for the purified compound at the analyte-ready stage, recorded before any analytical identity annotation is generated; examples include an internal code name, target scaffold name, or provisional compound label.
Observed physical form of the purified compound at the analyte-ready stage; examples include solid, oil, powder, or solution.

Chemical form of the analyte-ready compound as prepared for downstream use, recorded at the time of storage or transfer; examples include free base, hydrochloride salt, sodium salt, or other counterion form.
Condition used to store the purified compound before characterization or assay, recorded at the analyte-ready stage; examples include refrigerated, frozen, desiccated, or ambient.
Mass of purified analyte-ready compound available for downstream characterization and assays, reported in milligrams at the point of aliquoting or transfer.
Operational status of the purified compound immediately before analytical characterization begins, indicating whether the material is ready for NMR, mass spectrometry, and bioassay use.

nmr_capture.reasoning: The nmr_capture node is a Capture, so I included only instrument-configuration and session-level acquisition fields: spectrometer identity, nucleus, field strength, probe, pulse sequence, solvent, temperature, scan settings, and acquisition status. I excluded sample intrinsic properties because those belong to analyte_ready_compound, and I excluded raw spectrum file properties because those belong to nmr_spectrum. I also avoided the previously generated purity field and other upstream synthesis/purification metadata, focusing on what the operator configures or observes during the NMR measurement session.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the NMR spectrometer used for the measurement session, recorded as the active instrument description at acquisition time; for example Bruker, JEOL, or Agilent.
Model name or number of the NMR spectrometer used during the capture session, recorded at the time acquisition is configured; for example 'Avance III'.
Serial number of the NMR spectrometer used for the capture session, recorded from the instrument configuration at the time of acquisition; use a stable string identifier.
Observed nucleus targeted during the NMR acquisition session, recorded as the configured measurement channel; for example 1H, 13C, or 19F.
Operating magnetic field strength of the NMR spectrometer, reported in MHz equivalent for the proton frequency at acquisition time; typical values include 400, 500, or 600 MHz.
Probe type configured for the NMR measurement session, recorded at acquisition time; examples include inverse-detection, broadband, cryoprobe, or other probe configurations.

Pulse sequence used during the NMR acquisition session, recorded as the active experiment method at measurement time; examples include standard 1D proton or carbon experiments and vendor-specific sequence names.
Deuterated solvent used to dissolve the purified compound for the NMR measurement session, recorded as the configured sample solvent; examples include CDCl3, DMSO-d6, or D2O.

Sample temperature during the NMR acquisition session, reported in degrees Celsius as the actively controlled spectrometer sample temperature; typical values are near ambient but may be variable for exchange-sensitive compounds.
Total number of scans or transients collected during the NMR acquisition session, recorded as the active signal averaging setting at measurement time.
Total NMR acquisition time for the measurement session, reported in minutes from start to completion of the configured capture run.
Operational status of the NMR capture session after acquisition is complete; use this to indicate whether the run completed successfully and produced usable raw signal.

nmr_spectrum.reasoning: The nmr_spectrum node is a Signal, so I included only raw-file and technical signal properties: file format, location, size, dimensions, and basic quality/processing state. I excluded NMR instrument settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded molecular interpretation because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any sample or purity fields already assigned upstream, keeping this node focused on the raw data artefact itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw NMR data file generated by the capture session, recorded as the file artifact identifier at storage time; use a string such as 'sample123.fid' or an instrument export name.
File format of the raw NMR spectrum data, recorded for the stored artefact; examples include vendor-specific acquisition files, FID directories, or exported exchange formats.
Size of the raw NMR data artifact in bytes at the time of storage or transfer, reported as the raw file size for reuse and integrity checking.

Number of spectral or time-domain points contained in the raw NMR artefact, recorded as the technical data size of the signal output; typical values depend on acquisition parameters and may range from thousands to millions.
Total spectral width represented in the raw NMR signal, reported in ppm as stored or exported with the file; record the observed range covered by the acquisition.

Basic technical quality metric for the raw NMR spectrum, recorded after acquisition as a signal quality indicator; higher values generally indicate better usable signal, with practical ranges depending on nucleus and sample concentration.
Approximate number of discernible peaks or resonances in the raw NMR spectrum, recorded as a simple feature count for the signal artefact before identity interpretation.
Filesystem path, database location, or object-store key where the raw NMR spectrum is stored, recorded as the access location for the signal artefact.

Qualitative technical assessment of the raw NMR data integrity or usability, assigned to the signal artefact after acquisition; use this to flag whether the raw spectrum appears clean enough for downstream interpretation.

mass_spec_capture.reasoning: The mass_spec_capture node is a Capture, so I included only instrument configuration and acquisition-session fields: MS platform, manufacturer/model/serial, ionization, analyzer, polarity, scan range, resolution, source settings, and acquisition status. I excluded compound properties because those belong to analyte_ready_compound, and I excluded raw file technical properties because those belong to mass_spectrum. I also avoided repeating any NMR fields or downstream identity annotations, keeping this node limited to how the LC-MS measurement was configured and performed.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the mass spectrometer or LC-MS system used for the measurement session, recorded as the active instrument description at acquisition time; for example Thermo, Waters, Shimadzu, or Agilent.
Model name or number of the mass spectrometer used during the capture session, recorded at the time acquisition is configured; for example 'Q Exactive' or 'Triple Quad 5500'.
Serial number of the mass spectrometer used for the capture session, recorded from the instrument configuration at acquisition time; use a stable string identifier.

Ionization mode configured for the mass spectrometry session, recorded at acquisition time as the actively controlled source setting; examples include electrospray or atmospheric-pressure chemical ionization.
Polarity used during the mass spectrometry acquisition session, recorded as the configured source polarity; common values are positive or negative mode.
Mass analyzer type configured for the measurement session, recorded at acquisition time; examples include quadrupole, orbitrap, time-of-flight, or ion trap.
Mass-to-charge range acquired during the mass spectrometry session, reported as the active scan window in m/z at measurement time; for example 50-1000.
Instrument resolution setting used during acquisition, recorded as the active MS resolving power or nominal setting at measurement time; values depend on the analyzer and method.
Ion source or interface temperature during the LC-MS acquisition session, reported in degrees Celsius as the actively controlled source setting; typical values vary by instrument and method.

Desolvation or nebulizing gas flow setting used during the mass spectrometry acquisition session, recorded as the active source parameter; report in the instrument's standard flow unit or as a numeric setting in the local convention.
Total mass spectrometry acquisition time for the measurement session, reported in minutes from start to completion of the configured capture run.
Operational status of the mass spectrometry capture session after acquisition is complete; use this to indicate whether the run completed successfully and produced usable raw signal.

mass_spectrum.reasoning: The mass_spectrum node is a Signal, so I included only raw file and technical artefact fields: file format, size, storage location, dimensions, and basic quality indicators. I excluded acquisition settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded molecular identity or isotopic interpretation because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided duplicating any prior fields such as purity or instrument configuration, keeping the schema centered on the raw MS data artefact itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw mass spectrometry data file generated by the capture session, recorded as the file artifact identifier at storage time; use a string such as 'sample123.raw' or an instrument export name.
File format of the raw mass spectrum data, recorded for the stored artefact; examples include vendor-specific acquisition files, mzML, mzXML, or exported text formats.
Size of the raw mass spectrometry data artifact in bytes at the time of storage or transfer, reported as the raw file size for reuse and integrity checking.

Number of data points or scans represented in the raw mass spectrometry artefact, recorded as the technical data size of the signal output; typical values depend on acquisition mode and may range from hundreds to millions.
Observed or exported mass-to-charge range contained in the raw spectrum, recorded as the signal extent in m/z values for the raw artefact; for example '100-2000'.

Basic technical quality metric for the raw mass spectrum, recorded after acquisition as a signal quality indicator; higher values generally indicate better usable signal, with practical ranges depending on sample concentration and method.
Approximate number of discernible peaks or ions in the raw mass spectrum, recorded as a simple feature count for the signal artefact before interpretation.
Filesystem path, database location, or object-store key where the raw mass spectrum is stored, recorded as the access location for the signal artefact.

Qualitative technical assessment of the raw mass spectrometry data integrity or usability, assigned to the signal artefact after acquisition; use this to flag whether the raw spectrum appears clean enough for downstream interpretation.

nmr_identity_derivative.reasoning: The nmr_identity_derivative node is a Derivative, so I included only computed interpretation fields derived from the NMR spectrum: algorithm/method, annotation confidence, assigned structural features, predicted/confirmed identity labels, and output quality metrics. I excluded raw spectral file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded NMR acquisition settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node. I also avoided repeating any synthesis, purification, or sample identity fields already assigned earlier, keeping this node focused on the computed structural annotation itself.

md_schema.descr: Computational or manual interpretation method used to derive structural annotation from the NMR spectrum, recorded at the time the identity call is generated; examples include rule-based assignment, template matching, or expert curation.

Confidence score for the NMR-derived structural annotation, reported at the time the derivative is generated; use a numeric score in the local convention such as 0-1 or 0-100 to reflect assignment certainty.

Key structural features inferred from the NMR spectrum, recorded as a concise summary of the derivative output; examples include substitution pattern, functional groups, aromaticity, or stereochemical hints.

Provisional or confirmed compound identity inferred from the NMR spectrum, recorded as the derived structural annotation produced by the analysis step; use the compound name, scaffold, or text label assigned by the interpretation workflow.
Qualitative assessment of the NMR-derived identity call, recorded after interpretation is complete; use this to indicate whether the annotation is robust enough for downstream integration.

ms_identity_derivative.reasoning: The ms_identity_derivative node is a Derivative, so I included only computed interpretation fields derived from the mass spectrum: identity method, confidence, assigned molecular formula/mass-based annotations, adduct/isotope findings, and quality flags. I excluded capture settings and raw-file properties because those belong to the upstream Capture and Signal nodes, and I avoided repeating any prior compound identifiers or synthesis/purification metadata. The fields are centered on the computed MS-based molecular identity call that will later feed the integrated identity summary.

md_schema.descr: Computational or manual interpretation method used to derive molecular identity from the mass spectrum, recorded at the time the identity call is generated; examples include exact-mass matching, fragmentation matching, library search, or expert curation.

Confidence score for the MS-derived molecular identity annotation, reported at the time the derivative is generated; use a numeric score in the local convention such as 0-1 or 0-100 to reflect assignment certainty.
Molecular formula inferred from the mass spectrum, recorded as the derived formula annotation produced by the analysis step; use a standard chemical formula string such as C20H18ClN3O2.

Monoisotopic mass inferred or matched from the mass spectrum for the assigned compound, reported in daltons at the point of identity calling; typical values depend on the compound and should reflect the best-matched molecular ion.
Adduct species assigned from the mass spectrum, recorded as part of the identity interpretation output; examples include [M+H]+, [M-H]-, [M+Na]+, or neutral loss labels.

Score describing how well the observed isotope pattern matches the assigned molecular identity, recorded as a technical quality indicator for the mass-derived annotation; higher values indicate a better fit.
Qualitative assessment of the MS-derived identity call, recorded after interpretation is complete; use this to indicate whether the annotation is robust enough for downstream integration.

identity_integration.reasoning: The identity_integration node is a Process, so I included only computational integration details: software, version, repository, method, reconciliation rules, input references, runtime, and an output quality indicator. I excluded raw spectra and individual NMR/MS identity fields because those belong to the upstream Signal and Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final consolidated identity result because that belongs to the downstream compound_identity_summary node. I also avoided repeating any chemistry or capture settings already generated elsewhere, focusing on how the integration was performed and what software implementation was used.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or workflow used to reconcile NMR and mass spectrometry identity outputs, recorded at the time the integration process is run; for example a cheminformatics package or internal pipeline name.
Version of the integration software used for the identity reconciliation step, recorded as the exact release or commit version active during processing; for example '2.1.0'.

Repository, package source, or code location for the identity integration workflow, recorded so the computational method can be traced and reproduced; examples include a Git URL or internal repository label.

Algorithmic strategy used to combine the NMR and MS identity calls, recorded at the time of reconciliation; examples include rule-based consensus, weighted voting, confidence merging, or expert adjudication.

References to the upstream NMR and MS derivative records consumed by the integration step, recorded as process inputs; use identifiers or labels that point to the specific derivative outputs being reconciled.

Decision threshold used to accept or reject agreement between the NMR and MS identity calls, reported in the local score or similarity scale used by the integration workflow; typical values depend on the method and should be specified consistently.
Total runtime of the identity integration process, measured from workflow start to completion in minutes, recorded for computational performance tracking.
Overall outcome of the integration run, recorded after reconciliation is complete; use this to indicate whether the process produced a usable consolidated identity summary.

compound_identity_summary.reasoning: The compound_identity_summary node is a Derivative, so I included only computed integrated-result fields that summarize the candidate’s identity and characterization: consolidated compound label, structure/identity confidence, matched formula/mass features, key physicochemical descriptors, and an overall quality flag. I excluded raw NMR/MS signals and capture settings because those belong to upstream Signal/Capture nodes, and I excluded the integration software/process parameters because those belong to the upstream identity_integration Process node. I also avoided repeating any sample, reagent, or batch identifiers already generated earlier, focusing on the final interpreted compound-level output that downstream users will reuse.

md_schema.descr: Final consolidated name or label assigned to the herbicide candidate after identity integration, recorded as the derived compound identifier used for downstream reporting; examples include a validated project code or accepted scaffold name.

Overall confidence score for the integrated molecular identity assignment, reported at the time the summary is generated; use the local numeric scale such as 0-1 or 0-100 to reflect how strongly NMR and MS evidence support the final identity.

Final molecular formula accepted in the compound identity summary, recorded as the integrated formula annotation after reconciling NMR and mass spectrometry evidence; use a standard chemical formula string such as C20H18ClN3O2.
Final exact or monoisotopic mass associated with the identified herbicide candidate, reported in daltons in the integrated summary output; this value should reflect the reconciled molecular identity.

Concise summary of the key physicochemical properties associated with the identified compound, recorded in the integrated identity output; examples include polarity, inferred lipophilicity, or functional group class notes.

Qualitative indicator of whether the NMR and MS evidence were internally consistent in the integrated summary, recorded after reconciliation is complete; use this to flag agreement or conflicts among evidence sources.

Overall quality assessment of the integrated compound identity summary, recorded for downstream reuse and filtering; use this to indicate whether the summary is suitable for bioactivity interpretation and reporting.

assay_preparation.reasoning: The assay_preparation node is a Process, so I included only the operation details for preparing compounds for bioassay: dilution conditions, dispense format, assay plate/container setup, replicate scheme, vehicle/control handling, and process outcome. I excluded analyte-ready compound properties because those belong to the upstream Entity, and I excluded assay system intrinsic biology because that belongs to the downstream Entity node. I also avoided fields about the bioactivity measurement itself, since those belong to the later Capture and Signal nodes; this schema stays focused on how compounds were prepared and loaded into the assay system.

md_schema.descr: Name or short label of the assay preparation protocol used to dilute and dispense the purified compounds into the in vitro test system, recorded at the time the process is run; for example an SOP name or internal workflow label.

Overall dilution factor applied to the purified compound before dispensing into the assay system, recorded as the preparation step ratio; for example 10, 100, or a fold-dilution string if the local convention requires it.
Vehicle or carrier solvent used to solubilize or deliver the purified compound into the assay system, recorded at preparation time; examples include DMSO, water, or ethanol.

Final compound concentration in the assay system after dilution and dispensing, reported in the local assay concentration unit used by the workflow; include the unit in the recorded value convention, such as micromolar or nanomolar.
Volume of compound solution dispensed into each assay well, chamber, or reaction container, reported in microliters at the preparation stage.
Number of technical or biological replicates prepared for each compound condition in the assay system, recorded at the time the plate or assay layout is assembled.
Description of the positive, negative, and vehicle controls included during assay preparation, recorded as part of the assay layout and dispensing plan.
Overall status of the assay preparation run after dilution and dispensing are complete; use this to indicate whether the loaded assay system is ready for measurement.

assay_system.reasoning: The assay_system node is an Entity, so I included intrinsic properties of the prepared biological test system itself: organism/species source, assay target class, pathway or enzyme identity, matrix/cell state, plate or format, and preparation state. I excluded compound dosing and preparation parameters because those belong to the upstream assay_preparation Process, and I excluded capture settings and raw readouts because those belong to downstream Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating compound identity fields generated earlier, focusing on what the assay system is before measurement begins.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared in vitro assay system used as the biological test material; use a stable string such as 'AS-001'.
Name of the enzyme, pathway, or biological target represented by the assay system at the time it is prepared; examples include a specific plant enzyme or signaling pathway label.
Broad biological class of the assay target represented by the prepared system, recorded before measurement; examples distinguish enzyme assays from pathway or cell-based assays.
Plant species or source organism represented by the assay system, recorded as the biological origin of the prepared test material; examples include a crop or weed species name.

Prepared state of the assay material before measurement, recorded as the biological format of the test system; examples include live cells, lysate, membrane prep, enzyme extract, or reconstituted assay matrix.
Physical assay format of the prepared test system, recorded at preparation time; examples include 96-well plate, 384-well plate, cuvette-based, or imaging chamber format.
Operational state of the assay system immediately before measurement begins, indicating whether the biological test system is ready, equilibrated, or requires further preparation.
Total prepared amount of assay material available for measurement, reported in the workflow's local unit convention such as microliters, milliliters, or mass equivalent if applicable.

bioactivity_capture.reasoning: The bioactivity_capture node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields for the assay readout: reader/imaging hardware identity, detection mode, excitation/emission settings, integration time, plate type, and acquisition status. I excluded assay-system biology and compound concentration because those belong upstream to assay_system and assay_preparation, and I excluded raw readout file properties because those belong to bioactivity_signal. I also avoided repeating any previously generated field names, removing the conflicting acquisition_time_minutes field and keeping the schema focused on how the bioactivity measurement was configured and collected.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the plate reader, imaging system, or other assay measurement instrument used for the bioactivity session, recorded as the active instrument description at acquisition time; for example Molecular Devices, Tecan, PerkinElmer, or an imaging vendor.

Model name or number of the assay measurement instrument used during the capture session, recorded at the time acquisition is configured; for example a plate reader or imaging system model identifier.
Serial number of the assay measurement instrument used for the capture session, recorded from the instrument configuration at acquisition time; use a stable string identifier.
Detection mode configured for the bioactivity measurement session, recorded as the active readout method; examples include absorbance, fluorescence, luminescence, or imaging-based detection.

Excitation wavelength used during the bioactivity capture session, reported in nanometers when the selected detection mode requires illumination; record the actively configured setting at measurement time.

Emission wavelength used during the bioactivity capture session, reported in nanometers for fluorescence or luminescence-based readouts when applicable; record the actively configured detection channel.

Detector integration or exposure time used during the bioactivity acquisition session, reported in milliseconds as the actively controlled readout setting; typical values depend on the instrument and signal strength.
Plate or container type used during the bioactivity capture session, recorded as the active measurement format; examples include 96-well, 384-well, or imaging chamber plates.
Total duration of the bioactivity measurement session, reported in minutes from start to completion of the configured capture run.
Operational status of the bioactivity capture session after acquisition is complete; use this to indicate whether the run completed successfully and produced usable raw readout.

bioactivity_signal.reasoning: The bioactivity_signal node is a Signal, so I included only raw artefact and technical readout fields: file name/format, size, dimensions, storage location, and basic signal-quality metrics. I excluded assay plate setup and instrument settings because those belong to bioactivity_capture, and I excluded potency/toxicity interpretation because that belongs to potency_toxicity_analysis. I also avoided any previously used acquisition_time_minutes field and any sample biology fields, keeping the schema centered on the raw assay data object itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw bioactivity data file generated by the capture session, recorded as the file artifact identifier at storage time; use a string such as 'plate1.rds' or a vendor export name.
File format of the raw assay signal data, recorded for the stored artefact; examples include vendor export files, CSV, XLSX, JSON, or text-based exports.
Size of the raw bioactivity data artifact in bytes at the time of storage or transfer, reported as the raw file size for reuse and integrity checking.

Number of raw signal points, wells, frames, or time points contained in the assay readout artefact, recorded as the technical data size of the signal output; the exact interpretation depends on the assay format.
Primary dimensionality of the raw assay signal data, recorded as the shape of the artefact; for example single-point endpoint, time series, or image stack.
Filesystem path, database location, or object-store key where the raw bioactivity signal is stored, recorded as the access location for the signal artefact.

Basic technical quality metric for the raw assay signal, recorded after acquisition as a signal quality indicator; higher values generally indicate better usable readout, with practical ranges depending on the assay and detection mode.

Estimated background or baseline level present in the raw assay signal, recorded as a technical property of the signal artefact before biological interpretation; report in the assay's local intensity unit.

Qualitative technical assessment of the raw bioactivity data integrity or usability, assigned to the signal artefact after acquisition; use this to flag whether the raw readout appears clean enough for downstream analysis.

potency_toxicity_analysis.reasoning: The potency_toxicity_analysis node is a Process, so I included only computational analysis operation details: software identity/version/repository, analysis method, normalization/fit choices, input references, runtime, and process outcome. I excluded raw assay signal properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded the resulting potency/toxicity metrics themselves because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided repeating any earlier identity or capture fields, focusing on how the assay readouts were transformed into summary metrics.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis pipeline used to convert bioactivity readouts into potency and toxicity summaries, recorded at the time the process is run; for example an internal script suite or analysis package name.
Version of the analysis software used for potency and toxicity summarization, recorded as the exact release or commit version active during processing; for example '1.4.2'.

Repository, package source, or code location for the potency/toxicity analysis workflow, recorded so the computational method can be traced and reproduced; examples include a Git URL or internal repository label.

Algorithmic strategy used to convert assay readouts into potency and toxicity summaries, recorded at the time of analysis; examples include IC50 fitting, threshold-based scoring, dose-response modeling, or expert curation.

Data normalization approach applied before potency/toxicity estimation, recorded as the preprocessing method used on the assay readouts; examples include vehicle subtraction, z-score normalization, or percent-control scaling.

References to the upstream bioactivity signal records consumed by the analysis step, recorded as process inputs; use identifiers or labels that point to the specific raw assay outputs being summarized.
Total runtime of the potency/toxicity analysis process, measured from workflow start to completion in minutes, recorded for computational performance tracking.
Overall outcome of the analysis run, recorded after computation is complete; use this to indicate whether the process produced usable potency and toxicity summaries.

potency_toxicity_summary.reasoning: The potency_toxicity_summary node is a Derivative, so I included only computed result fields: potency metrics, toxicity metrics, fit/assay-response summaries, confidence, and summary quality. I excluded raw assay signals and capture settings because those belong to the upstream Signal and Capture nodes, and I excluded analysis software/process parameters because those belong to the upstream potency_toxicity_analysis Process node. I also avoided repeating earlier compound identity fields, keeping this node focused on the derived efficacy and toxicity characterization for downstream selection and ranking.

md_schema.descr: Primary potency metric produced by the bioactivity analysis, recorded as the derived efficacy measure for the compound; examples include IC50, EC50, percent inhibition at a fixed dose, or a custom activity score.
Numeric value of the derived potency metric, reported in the same unit or scale used by the analysis workflow; for example micromolar IC50 values or percent inhibition scores.
Unit or scale associated with the potency metric value, recorded alongside the derived result; examples include uM, nM, percent, or score units.

Primary toxicity metric produced by the bioactivity analysis, recorded as the derived safety or adverse-effect measure for the compound; examples include cytotoxicity score, viability reduction, or selectivity index proxy.
Numeric value of the derived toxicity metric, reported in the same unit or scale used by the analysis workflow; for example percent viability, toxicity score, or index value.
Unit or scale associated with the toxicity metric value, recorded alongside the derived result; examples include percent, ratio, or score units.
Quality indicator for the fitted dose-response or response-summary model used to derive potency and toxicity metrics, recorded as a technical confidence or fit statistic after analysis.
Direction of the compound effect summarized from the assay data, recorded as the net response direction in the derived result; examples include inhibitory, activating, neutral, or mixed.
Overall confidence score for the derived potency and toxicity summary, recorded at the time the summary is generated; use the local numeric scale such as 0-1 or 0-100 to indicate result reliability.

Qualitative assessment of the derived potency and toxicity summary, recorded after analysis is complete; use this to indicate whether the summary is robust enough for downstream selection and reporting.

selectivity_assessment.reasoning: The selectivity_assessment node is a Process, so I included only the joint-analysis operation details: software identity/version/repository, assessment method, weighting or decision rules, input references, runtime, and outcome status. I excluded the compound identity and potency/toxicity contents themselves because those belong to the upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final selectivity conclusion because that belongs to the downstream selectivity_report node. I also avoided duplicating earlier analysis software or capture fields, focusing on how the integrated evaluation was performed.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or workflow used to combine compound identity and bioactivity summaries for herbicide selectivity assessment, recorded at the time the process is run; for example an internal decision pipeline or analysis package name.
Version of the selectivity assessment software used for the joint analysis step, recorded as the exact release or commit version active during processing; for example '3.0.1'.
Repository, package source, or code location for the selectivity assessment workflow, recorded so the method can be traced and reproduced; examples include a Git URL or internal repository label.

Algorithmic or expert strategy used to combine identity and bioactivity evidence into a selectivity assessment, recorded at the time of analysis; examples include rule-based ranking, weighted scoring, multicriteria decision analysis, or expert curation.

Weighting or prioritization scheme applied to identity and bioactivity evidence during selectivity assessment, recorded as the decision logic used by the workflow; describe how the different inputs were balanced.

References to the upstream identity and potency/toxicity summary records consumed by the selectivity assessment step, recorded as process inputs; use identifiers or labels that point to the specific derivative outputs being integrated.
Total runtime of the selectivity assessment process, measured from workflow start to completion in minutes, recorded for computational performance tracking.
Overall outcome of the selectivity assessment run, recorded after computation is complete; use this to indicate whether the process produced a usable selectivity evaluation.

selectivity_report.reasoning: The selectivity_report node is a Derivative, so I included only the final computed evaluation fields: selectivity score/classification, agricultural utility ranking, integrated confidence, key supporting criteria, and report quality. I excluded the upstream identity and potency/toxicity summaries because those belong to their own derivative nodes, and I excluded the selectivity assessment software/process parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also avoided repeating earlier sample or reagent identifiers, keeping this node focused on the final integrated decision output for herbicide candidate prioritization.

md_schema.descr: Final numeric score representing the compound's selectivity in the integrated herbicide evaluation, recorded as the derived ranking value after combining identity and bioactivity evidence; use the local scoring scale defined by the workflow.
Final categorical selectivity call assigned to the compound in the integrated report, recorded after assessment of potency and off-target toxicity; use this to classify candidate suitability.

Overall rating of the compound's potential utility for agricultural application, recorded in the final integrated report after considering potency, selectivity, and safety; use a categorical ranking defined by the workflow.

Confidence score for the final integrated selectivity report, reported at the time the derivative is generated; use the local numeric scale such as 0-1 or 0-100 to reflect certainty in the final decision.

Concise summary of the main criteria used to justify the final integrated selectivity report, such as potency threshold, toxicity margin, and identity confidence; record this as text for interpretability.

Qualitative assessment of consistency between identity, potency, and selectivity evidence in the final report, recorded after integration is complete; use this to flag agreement or conflicts among upstream summaries.
Overall quality assessment of the final selectivity report, recorded for downstream filtering and reuse; use this to indicate whether the result is robust enough for candidate prioritization.
